question: What is the main point of health planning in a community?

options.A: Identifying health problems and using resources to meet goals
options.B: Reducing the total number of patients admitted to wards
options.C: Building more private hospitals in urban centers
options.D: Increasing the salary of medical and nursing personnel

explanation: You've got this! Health planning is simply finding out what health issues a community faces and figuring out how to use available resources to solve them. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why is a nurse's voice so important when planning healthcare in places with limited resources?

options.A: Nurses decide which pharmaceutical companies win government contracts
options.B: Nurses hold the highest political office in health ministries
options.C: Nurses understand practical frontline needs and realistic interventions
options.D: Nurses are solely responsible for funding hospital budgets

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses work side-by-side with patients every single day, they know what actually works on the ground. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which method do nurses usually use to gather health facts directly from a community?

options.A: Conducting home visits and community dialogues
options.B: Waiting for international health organizations to send reports
options.C: Consulting only with the federal minister of health

explanation: Great choice! Going directly into the community through visits and talks gives nurses a clear picture of real health conditions. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is a big drawback of looking only at hospital records to assess a community's health?

options.A: It only includes data about elderly male patients
options.B: It misses people who cannot afford or access hospital care
options.C: It takes too much time for the nursing staff to read
options.D: It contains too many details about infectious diseases

explanation: Exactly. Hospital records only capture those who manage to reach the facility, leaving out the many sick people stuck at home due to distance or poverty. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the main reason nurses and planners must set priorities?

options.B: All health problems cost the exact same amount to treat
options.C: Government policies forbid buying new medical equipment
options.D: Doctors refuse to participate in budgeting meetings

explanation: That's right! Since funds, drugs, and hands are never endless, we have to choose which urgent needs to tackle first. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h3)

question: A clinic has very little money and must choose between buying new office chairs or running a child immunization drive. What should come first?

options.A: Splitting the money evenly so neither project is fully completed
options.B: Returning the funds to the government to avoid making a choice
options.C: The office chairs because administrative comfort improves staff mood
options.D: The child immunization drive because it prevents disease outbreaks

explanation: You nailed it! Protecting kids from deadly diseases brings a huge public health win compared to upgrading office furniture. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h3)

question: What does creating a healthcare policy actually involve?

options.A: Cleaning hospital wards after a surgical procedure
options.B: Diagnosing rare tropical diseases in a laboratory
options.C: Administering daily medication to individual patients
options.D: Creating guidelines and rules that govern health delivery

explanation: Policies are simply the official rules and guidelines that shape how healthcare systems are run. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why should nurses be involved when high-level health decisions are being made?

options.A: It allows nurses to manage hospital finances without auditing
options.B: It ensures policies reflect practical realities of patient care
options.C: It guarantees that doctors will no longer work in hospitals
options.D: It stops the government from spending money on medication

explanation: Spot on! When nurses have a seat at the table, the resulting rules make sense for everyday clinical work. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h4)

question: What does cost-effective healthcare mean in simple terms?

options.A: Charging patients double the price for basic nursing care
options.B: Achieving the best health outcomes with the fewest resources
options.C: Employing only student nurses to avoid paying salaries
options.D: Refusing to buy any modern drugs or equipment

explanation: You got it! Cost-effectiveness is about getting the best possible health results without wasting hard-earned money or supplies. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is a great example of cost-effective healthcare planning?

options.A: Purchasing expensive imported machines instead of servicing local ones
options.B: Waiting until patients are critically ill before treating them
options.C: Focusing heavily on preventive health education in the community
options.D: Throwing away opened medication vials at the end of every shift

explanation: Brilliant! Stopping a disease before it starts is always much cheaper and easier than treating late-stage sickness. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h5)

question: What happens during the implementation stage of a health plan?

options.A: The health committee writes down initial budget guesses
options.B: All nurses retire and hand over duties to administrators
options.C: The community is surveyed to see if they want a clinic
options.D: The planned health programs and services are put into action

explanation: Implementation is the active phase where your written plans finally turn into real care for people. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h6)

question: Why is it important for a nurse manager to stay flexible while running a program?

options.A: Staff members prefer working without a fixed schedule
options.B: Government rules require changing the budget every week
options.C: It stops patients from asking questions about their care
options.D: Unforeseen challenges like transport breakdowns often occur

explanation: That's true! Unexpected hurdles happen all the time in real life, so a good manager adapts quickly to keep things moving. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is ongoing tracking, while evaluation assesses final results
options.B: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses on buildings
options.C: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.D: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is completely free

explanation: You've got it! Monitoring happens step-by-step as the project runs, while evaluation looks at the big picture after it's done. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h7)

question: Why does nursing leadership need to carry out regular program evaluations?

options.A: It reveals if the interventions are actually improving health outcomes
options.B: It ensures that no patient ever complains about the hospital
options.C: It proves that administrative staff are smarter than clinical nurses
options.D: It gives staff a reason to stop working for several months

explanation: Spot on! Evaluation tells us whether our hard work and resources actually solved the health problem we targeted. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing Nigerian nurses in health planning?

options.A: Excessive availability of well-trained nursing staff
options.B: Brain drain and migration of healthcare professionals
options.C: Poor infrastructure and unreliable electricity supply
options.D: Inadequate funding for primary healthcare programs

explanation: That's right! Nigeria actually faces serious nursing shortages due to migration, not a surplus of staff. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h8)

question: How can Nigerian nurses break through barriers that keep them out of health planning rooms?

options.A: By ignoring hospital management and making independent laws
options.B: By working entirely in private clinics without government oversight
options.C: By building strong professional advocacy and gaining leadership training
options.D: By refusing to care for patients until they are given management titles

explanation: Brilliant! Standing up for our profession, sharpening our leadership skills, and bringing solid evidence helps us earn our rightful seat at the table. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h8)
